metaDescription: Boulder and armour stone retaining walls for Strathroy rural and residential properties, natural look with engineered drainage. Free written quotes.
h1: Natural Stone Retaining Walls in Strathroy, Ontario
intro: Farm and acreage properties around Strathroy often have room for a natural stone wall to do double duty, holding back a grade change while looking like it belongs on the land.

blocks.text: Boulder and armour stone walls suit larger rural lots particularly well, where a more rugged, natural appearance fits the surrounding landscape better than a manufactured block product. They also work for informal terracing along a sloped driveway or field edge.
On residential subdivision lots, stone is used more often for a smaller feature wall or garden border than the primary retaining structure.

items.title: Base preparation
items.text: Compacted base sized to the stone weight, with equipment access planned for larger armour stone.

items.title: Setting the stones
items.text: Larger stones placed first with proper batter, working up in courses.

items.title: Drainage
items.text: Drainage stone and filter fabric behind the wall, same standard as our other systems.

items.title: Backfill and finish
items.text: Compacted in lifts, site graded and cleaned up on completion.

blocks.text: Armour stone gives the most structural capacity for taller sections. Smaller boulders or fieldstone suit garden borders and low, informal grade changes.
The Municipality of Strathroy-Caradoc applies the same roughly one metre threshold to stone walls as other materials. We handle the permit application for you.

For farm and acreage properties near Strathroy, we often select stone that complements the existing rural character of the land, larger armour stone for structural sections and smaller fieldstone for borders and informal areas.
If you're still weighing stone against other materials for your project, /how-to-choose-retaining-wall-material covers the full comparison.

sections.heading: Boulder Wall Placement on Sloped Fields

blocks.text: Boulder walls on sloped agricultural land near Strathroy are typically set with a shallower batter than a formal residential wall, following the natural line of the slope rather than a strict vertical structure.

faqs.q: Is natural stone suitable for a farm property near Strathroy?
faqs.a: Yes, it's a common choice for grade changes along driveways and field edges where a natural appearance fits the property.

faqs.q: How heavy is armour stone, and does it need equipment to place?
faqs.a: Yes, armour stone typically requires equipment for safe and accurate placement, which we bring to every stone wall project.

faqs.q: Can I combine stone with a timber or block wall on the same property?
faqs.a: Yes, different wall types can be used for different areas of the same property based on function and appearance.

faqs.q: What's the typical cost of a natural stone wall near Strathroy?
faqs.a: It depends on stone type, size and wall length. We provide a free written quote after assessing the site.

faqs.q: Does stone suit a working farm property, or is it mainly decorative?
faqs.a: Both. Armour stone provides genuine structural capacity for grade changes while still fitting the visual character of a rural or agricultural property.

faqs.q: Are boulder walls built differently than a formal stone wall?
faqs.a: Often with a shallower batter that follows the natural slope, particularly on agricultural land, compared to a more formal residential stone wall.

faqs.q: Will a stone wall need different maintenance than a block wall on my property?
faqs.a: Very little maintenance either way, provided drainage was installed correctly. Stone doesn't have the joint sealant or cap adhesive that some block products use, so there's slightly less to inspect over the years.
